citeAs: Seamless Communication, Barrault, L., Chung, Y.-A., Coria Meglioli, M., Dale, D., Dong, N., Duquenne, P.-A., et al. (2023). SeamlessM4T: Massively Multilingual & Multimodal Machine Translation. arXiv:2308.11596.
creator: Seamless Communication, Loïc Barrault, Yu-An Chung, Mariano Coria Meglioli, David Dale, Ning Dong, Paul-Ambroise Duquenne, Hady Elsahar, Hongyu Gong, Kevin Heffernan, and others (Meta AI)
description: SeamlessAlign is the largest open dataset for multimodal translation, totaling 470,000 hours of automatically aligned speech translations. This variant (asahi417_seamless-align-enA-hiA.speaker-embedding.xlsr-2b) is a speaker-embedding subset for the English-Hindi language pair, derived using XLSR-2B speech representations. SeamlessAlign was created through parallel data mining using SONAR multimodal embeddings to align speech and text across languages.
name: SeamlessAlign (English-Hindi speaker embedding subset, XLSR-2B)
rai:dataBiases: Gender representation analysis shows masculine lexica are overrepresented compared to feminine in SeamlessAlign mined data (as shown in Figure 23 of the paper). The dataset is derived from web-crawled audio which may reflect existing societal biases. Language coverage is skewed toward higher-resource languages, with Hindi classified as a medium-resource language. The mining approach uses global mining rather than local mining, which may miss domain-specific parallel content.
rai:dataCollection: SeamlessAlign was created through automated parallel data mining. Starting with 4 million hours of raw audio from publicly available crawled web data, the pipeline applied speech language identification (LID), audio segmentation using Voice Activity Detection (VAD) with over-segmentation, and SONAR multimodal embeddings to mine aligned speech-text and speech-speech pairs. Mining was performed using a margin criterion with the Stopes library, comparing embeddings via FAISS-based similarity search. For the English-Hindi direction, speech encoders were trained on human-provided ASR transcriptions (148 hours for Hindi) and used to project speech into the SONAR embedding space for mining.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw audio data: approximately 4 million hours of audio from a publicly available repository of crawled web data, with approximately 1 million hours in English. Text data: the same sentence-segmented dataset deployed in NLLB, using the same data sources, cleaning, and filtering steps. For Hindi specifically, 15,118 hours of raw audio were available for mining, with 150 hours of human-provided ASR transcriptions used to train the speech encoder.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Dataset released August 22nd, 2023 (model card date). Collection timeframe for underlying web-crawled audio not explicitly stated.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Passive Data Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to 37 target languages (out of the 100 SeamlessM4T languages); scaling to all 100 languages is left for future work. Mining produces noisy alignments requiring filtering. The over-segmentation strategy (8x increase in segments) introduces noise in the embedding space. Pause-based segments may not align with semantically coherent sentences. Global mining does not leverage knowledge of longer speech chunks. The dataset shows masculine representation predominance over feminine in gender analysis. Personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated from web-crawled data.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Mining used a margin criterion score with threshold set at 1.15 (adapted from the 1.06 used for LASER-based bitext mining). FAISS library was used for efficient large-scale GPU-based similarity search. Global mining was performed comparing all speech segments in one language against all segments in another. The metadata for the full unfiltered 470,000 hours (up to Sonar threshold of 1.15) is open-sourced, allowing users to tune the threshold for their own use cases. For the SeamlessM4T model training, only the top 400 hours per X-eng direction and top 200 hours per eng-X direction based on Sonar alignment scores were used.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio preprocessing steps: (1) deduplication of audio file URLs, (2) downloading and resampling at 16KHz, (3) filtering non-speech data with a bespoke audio event detection (AED) model, (4) Voice Activity Detection (VAD) segmentation using Silero VAD, (5) over-segmentation to create overlapping splits, (6) speech language identification (LID) filtering with a threshold per language such that p(correct|score) > p(incorrect|score), rejecting ~8% of data. Text preprocessing followed NLLB pipeline using the Stopes library. LID filtering improved F1 by ~3% while retaining 92.1% coverage.
rai:dataSocialImpact: SeamlessAlign enables training of speech translation systems that can improve world-readiness and information access, particularly for low-resource language communities. The dataset supports development of technologies that can assist those with limited literacy or visual impairments. However, the authors note that access could make groups with lower digital literacy more vulnerable to misinformation or online scams if misappropriated. The training data was mined from publicly available web sources, and personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated despite data cleaning efforts.
rai:dataUseCases: Primary intended use is training multilingual and multimodal speech translation systems, including speech-to-text translation (S2TT), speech-to-speech translation (S2ST), and automatic speech recognition (ASR). The metadata is open-sourced to allow the community to rebuild SeamlessAlign and use it for their own purposes, with the ability to tune the Sonar alignment threshold to balance dataset size and alignment quality.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SONAR speech and text encoders (teacher-student trained, based on w2v-BERT 2.0 front-end and NLLB-1.3B text encoder); ECAPA-TDNN-based speech language identification model (LID100) trained on VoxLingua107 data; Silero VAD for voice activity detection and audio segmentation; bespoke audio event detection (AED) model for non-speech filtering; FAISS library for large-scale similarity search; XLS-R-1B for discrete acoustic unit extraction (35th layer features, k-means with K=10000 centroids).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The training data was mined from publicly available sources on the web. Although heavy investment in data cleaning was made, personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated, as acknowledged in the model card ethical considerations section.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: SeamlessAlign is an automatically mined dataset with no human annotations per item; alignment scores are computed automatically via SONAR similarity.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: SeamlessAlign uses automated mining with no human annotators for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: SeamlessAlign is automatically mined; no human annotation analysis is applicable.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: SeamlessAlign uses automated mining pipelines (Stopes library), not a human annotation platform.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: SeamlessAlign is automatically mined with no human annotation protocol.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling for SeamlessAlign beyond the LID filtering that rejects ~8% of data for quality.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described for SeamlessAlign; missing or low-quality data is filtered out rather than imputed.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan described for SeamlessAlign beyond the initial open-source release of metadata.
